title: The British & Irish Lions: Rugby's Greatest Adventure
summary: Every four years, the best players from four rugby nations set aside their rivalries to become one team. The British & Irish Lions tour is unique in world sport — a tradition that creates bonds, legends, and heartbreaks unlike anything else in the game.
content:
There is nothing else in sport quite like the British & Irish Lions. Four nations — England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland — who spend most of the rugby year trying to beat each other, who play in the Six Nations with fierce national pride, who celebrate when their rivals lose — come together every four years to form a single touring team. Players who were opponents in February become teammates in June. A Lions shirt, earned against the Southern Hemisphere's best, is considered by many players to be the highest honour in the game.

The Lions have been touring since 1888, making them one of sport's oldest touring traditions. They have toured Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa — the three nations that have historically dominated the southern hemisphere — and the matches against those national sides have produced some of rugby union's most dramatic moments.

The Selection Process

Being selected for the Lions is not guaranteed by any amount of club success or even international form. The head coach — appointed specifically for each tour — must look across four different rugby cultures and pick players who will not just perform individually, but gel as a team in the space of a few weeks.

The selection calls that go unmade are as famous as the calls that are made. Players who seemed certainties are left out; unexpected names appear on the list. And then 36-odd players, many of whom have been fierce rivals, must become a team fast enough to test the best rugby nations in the world.

Being a Lion means you've been recognised by all four nations as one of the best in the British Isles. That means more than any individual cap, because it's your peers and rivals saying it, not just your own fans.

The 1971 New Zealand Tour

The Lions have beaten the All Blacks in a series only once — in 1971, under the coaching of Carwyn James and the captaincy of John Dawes. It remains one of rugby's most remarkable achievements. The Lions won the series 2-1 with one match drawn, in New Zealand, against a team that had lost only one home series in decades.

That squad — Barry John, Gareth Edwards, Willie John McBride, JPR Williams — is considered the greatest Lions team ever assembled. They played rugby that New Zealand had never seen, running the All Blacks off the park in a way that changed how the game was thought about in both hemispheres.

Modern Lions Tours

The 2021 tour to South Africa, played without crowds due to COVID-19 restrictions, ended in a 1-1 draw with the World Champions — a series that many felt the Lions deserved to win. The 2025 tour to Australia will be watched by rugby fans worldwide with the same mixture of hope and anxiety that has characterised every Lions tour for over a century.

The Lions remain what they have always been: rugby's greatest adventure. Four rivals, one team, three Tests, and the chance to do something that only comes around once every four years.
